To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CTCT motif in the plant promoters does not seem to mediate in the response to the MF.

1) the CTCT motif in the promoter regions is not randomly distributed in both potato and thale cresse; 2) the closer these CTCT motifs to the transcription initiation, the smaller distance is between the CTCT motifs; 3) the MF did not influence gene transcription in the potato plants with three promoters containing from 3–12 CTCT motifs.
CTCT motifs are not randomly distributed in plant promoter sequences and do not mediate the MF influence on gene transcription in the studied potato promoters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the universality of the CTCT motif mechanism in plants.
the universality of MFs’ influence on transcription via CTCT motifs in plants.
the universality of the CTCT motif mechanism of the influence of MF on transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MFs do not influence transcription via the CTCT motif in the promoters of three genes from potato and thale cresse.
the CTCT motif in the promoters of plants is not responsible for the response to MFs.
the MFs do not influence the gene transcription via the CTCT motif.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MFs can potentially influence the transcription of plant genes, but the CTCT motif in the promoter regions is not the main mediator of this process.
the CTCT motif in the plant promoter is not a universal regulator of gene transcription in response MFs.
the mechanism of MF influence on gene transcription is species-specific.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CTCT motif does influence gene transcription in plants, but the mechanism is different from that in animals.
the CTCT motif is not universal for the regulation of gene transcription by MFs and the mechanism of MF influence on transcription is species-specific.
the mechanism of gene transcription regulation in response to MF is not universal and may be specific to certain genes and/or species.
